routing_warnings.description: The dark treatment, purple background, hero emphasis, logo treatment, and screen imagery concern the landing-page composition rather than the reusable token requirement.

The active-node accent, node glow, wizard dimensions, responsive gaps, and chevron asset are wizard-specific styling evidence; only the reusable color and interaction-state requests are retained here.
The requested token sheet, font files, and maximum content width are design-system inputs better owned by the website design-token Requirement.
The delivered files specifically implement the updated desktop and mobile footer and should not be duplicated under the broader handoff Requirement.
The explicit website-chrome change is the addition of a header menu; the message does not state that the new pages change or verify the shared visual treatment.
The request to rough out code for the additional pages concerns implementation handoff rather than the sign-in page's visual styling.
The request to send the proposed Sign In file is a deliverable handoff request rather than a change to the visual styling requirement.
The client accepts rough coding for the additional pages; this changes the implementation-handoff obligation rather than the provisioning wizard's visual styling.
The placement and interaction of shell-level and application-level collapsible panels belongs to Console navigation structure rather than general shell visual styling.
The proposal to nest application items within one side panel concerns Console navigation structure.
The client's rejection of competing panels on opposite sides changes the Console navigation structure.
The requested decisions about Console button color, shape, size, and icons belong to the separate button-styling Requirement.
The proposed branded colors and rounded or pill-shaped treatment concern Console button styling.
The reported removal of top navigation concerns the independently defined website header-navigation Requirement.
The reported removal of footer links concerns the independently defined website-footer Requirement.
The landing-page zip and styling package primarily evidence the implementation handoff rather than a new visual-design transition.
The client's explicit acceptance of removing header navigation should also be evaluated under the header-navigation Requirement.
The requested footer content, links, social icons, copyright, and solid background concern the website-footer Requirement.
The overlapping hero elements and added intermediate breakpoint concern responsive layout behavior rather than the landing page's visual-design requirement.
The submitted design is described only as a Console UI and does not specifically entail implementation of the button treatment.
The client reports finalizing the Console's general look-and-feel and layout without identifying the button treatment.

missing_requirement_candidates.suggested_title: Landing Page Sign-Up Call to Action
missing_requirement_candidates.description: The required sign-up button is an independently testable landing-page behavior not represented in the frozen inventory.
The single-page section structure and placement of the How It Works sequence are content-architecture decisions independent of visual styling, responsive behavior, and page chrome.
